S0: This is Myrosta on your phone. Seven things you'll do with it, from the first text to your next leave request. We'll do each one together, as it happens.
S1: Your invite comes as a text or an email. Tap the link, choose mobile or email, and ask for a code. There's no password: the code is the password, and this phone stays signed in. You land on My shifts. One more thing, once: Share, then Add to Home Screen, so Myrosta opens like an app.
S2a: The text says the round is open. Open Book shifts and tap a day. At the top, AM or PM. Below it, one chip per zone: Open means it's yours to take, and a taken one shows who has it. Your picks wait in the basket at the bottom. Add a few more days, then Confirm. The receipt is the thing to look at: that's your share, booked. Your share is set by your admin, per fortnight, and the counter shows how much of it you've used. If a colleague confirmed the same slot a moment before you, you're told which pick didn't go in, and you pick again. When the round closes, your admin publishes, and the whole roster lands on your phone.
S2b: Your roster is live from launch week and live all cycle. Your manager places much of each fortnight; you book what is still open, whenever you need to, within your share. Tap a day, choose the shift type, and tap a zone marked Open: it's booked there and then, and the receipt counts your share. When your manager posts a gap, or a colleague gives a shift away, it appears under Open shifts on My shifts and in your notifications. Tap Claim: the first person free to take it gets it, with the same checks as any booking. Days that have passed are locked.
S3: My shifts is your week at a glance: the next shift, the next seven days, the whole cycle, and your counts. Tap Calendar. Add to calendar puts the dates you choose in your phone's calendar; Live calendar gives you a link that keeps itself up to date, so it sits in the calendar your family already shares. And the evening before each shift, Myrosta texts you, in case the week ran away. Share sends your week as a message.
S4: Something's come up for Saturday. Tap the shift, then Swap it. Two ways: with a colleague, where you pick them and one of their shifts and they agree first; or Ask everyone. The screen says how many colleagues it goes to: those free that day who have a shift you could take. Add a note, and ask. Offers arrive under Requests. Accept the one you want; the others close by themselves, and it goes to your admin, who approves it with the cover in front of them. If a colleague asks, Swaps wanted lists the asks you could take: choose one of your shifts and send the offer.
S5: Further out than your group's notice period, you can simply remove a shift: it goes straight to the group as an open shift. Inside the notice period the day sheet tells you how many days are left, and gives you three ways: offer it to the group, and you're off when a colleague takes it; ask to come off with a reason, and your admin decides; or swap it. You can do all three, and whichever happens first wins. A day you can't work at all: mark it unavailable, so nobody expects you. That isn't leave: it never reaches pay, and a shift you already hold that day stays until you swap it or offer it.
S6: Requests, then Request leave: the dates, the type, a reason, send. Your admin sees the whole picture, the leave you've taken, who else is away, the cap, and approves or declines; if they ask a question, the request says it needs your reply. Once approved, any shift you had those days comes off and is offered to the group. You'll know before lunch.
S7: The bell tells you about approvals, swaps, open shifts and messages; switch on alerts and they reach your lock screen. Day board shows who's on today and where. Fairness shows everyone the same table of who carries the weekends and evenings. And Help sends your question straight to the people who built it.
A0: You run the roster. This is a whole cycle in Myrosta, as you'll live it: set it up, invite your people, open it, run it day to day, and pay it. Seven minutes, your hands on it the whole time.
A1: Everything about a cycle lives on the cycle, so the next one starts from a copy and nothing you set now leaks into the past. Dates first. Zones: one slot per half-day each. Cover: the minimum and maximum per half. Shift types: rename AM and PM, add the rest; a type that fills both halves is a full shift and counts two toward a share. Notice to come off: inside it, staff can't simply drop a shift. Quota and fairness: each person's share, per fortnight. Mode: rounds, where everyone books in a window and you publish; or rolling, live once and live all cycle. Then the group's own card: its name, its logo, and the open-shift marketplace, so a shift someone drops reaches the whole group. Get started in Settings shows anything still unticked.
A2: Every person needs a mobile or an email: that's how they sign in and how reminders reach them. Add them one by one, or import the staff list from a spreadsheet. Access control decides who may sign in: sync the allow-list, then Invite your staff. The invites are real texts and emails, so send them when you mean it. Make admin gives a colleague the same keys as you.
A3a: Open the round, and the roster lands on every phone at once. Then you watch. The grid fills itself over the week, and a red tag shows any half that's still short. When the round closes, publish: everyone's told, and that's the roster of record. You can still change any cell afterwards; on a live roster each change asks for a reason and is written to the audit log with your name and the time.
A3b: On a rolling roster you place first. Tap a cell: off, shift or leave, the type, the zone, and the real hours if they differ from the type. Gaps show as needing cover: assign someone, or broadcast the slot as an open shift for the group to claim. Pre-fill the rest places people fairly into every short half, keeping to the rules; check it before you trust it. If you want to place everything yourself for a while, set a booking window before you go live. Then Go live: everyone's told, the app is the record, and the spreadsheet is never imported again.
A4: Requests is where the roster asks you things, each with what you need to decide. A swap arrives once the colleague has agreed, or once an ask-everyone offer has been accepted: the two shifts side by side, approve or decline, and the roster moves. An ask to come off shows the notice left, the reason, the cover without them, and everyone free that day with a tap-to-call; keep them on, or let them off and the gap goes to the group. A leave request comes with the whole picture: their EFT, the leave they've taken, this request in hours, who else is away, and the cap. Approve, decline, or ask a question, which comes back with their reply. Approving takes their shifts off those days and offers each to the group.
A5: The Day board is today: cover per half, who's in which zone, and who's on right now. Week shows the shape of the week. Messages reach everyone or one person, inside the app. And the audit log records every change, by person or by kind, with a name and a time, and downloads as a spreadsheet when anyone asks what happened.
A6: Fairness shows the same table to everyone: who is carrying the tough shifts, so the conversation is about the numbers. When it's time to pay, Roster, then Export. The grid as Excel or CSV for printing and sharing; and where the payroll export is switched on, the payroll file in your template's columns and the RosterOn workbook, one row per shift with the real start, finish and hours, call-ins included. An unavailable day is never a pay row.
A7: Each staff group is its own roster, with its own people, zones, cover and settings, under one hospital. Switch roster moves between them. Publish to the department board, in each group, and the Day board's Whole department shows every group side by side, today or any day in the next fortnight, printable as the handover sheet. The board carries only names, slots and times, never contacts, pay or requests.
A8: Two phones book the same slot: the one that reached the server first keeps it, the other is told. An ask, an offer or a swap closes itself when its shift moves, and whoever offered is told. Clear the roster always asks first, with counts. A refused save says what would break and what to do instead. Someone can't sign in: check their mobile or email, then sync the allow-list. And Help sends a note straight to the developer.
M1: From an hour before your shift, tap Clock in. Your phone asks for its location once; the tap goes through either way. At reception you can scan the poster instead. Inside the grace band nothing more happens: your rostered hours stand. Outside it, your shift says waiting for your manager, then the hours they approve. Forget to clock out and the record closes itself at the end of the day. Myrosta keeps only the time of your tap and how far you were from the clinic.
M2: At sites that log on-call after the event: tap today, then I was called in. From and To are filled in for you; set them to the hours you worked, inside the window, and save. It shows on the roster and beside your counts, it's paid with the hours you logged, and you can change or remove it until the end of tomorrow.
M3: Where your admins allow it, a shift can carry your own start and finish. Book it as usual: a tap books the shift with the type's hours. Then open it again, tap Change hours, set your start or your finish, and Save; Same as the type puts them back. Pay, the calendar and the reminder use your hours; cover and your share still count the half.
M4: Where several groups share a hospital, Day board has Whole department: one card per group, today or any day in the next fortnight, who's on right now marked. The other groups see only your name, your slot and its times, never your contacts, pay or requests.
AM1: Switch the clock on and your people clock in and out from their phone or the poster at reception; nothing is paid until you decide. Set the site standing at the clinic, the radius, the grace band, print the poster, and tick it on. Anything outside the grace band comes to Hours to approve: the rostered hours against the clocked ones, the proposal, and the flags. Approve writes the proposal as the shift's own hours for pay; decline keeps the roster. The clock report gives the pay office one row per person and day.
AM2: Where on-call is logged after the event, add a window that's chosen when booked: the range, the usual length, and let staff log their own. A consultant taps I was called in on the day; you can add, change or remove one for anyone from the roster cell, and you're told each time. A call-in takes no zone, never counts as cover, and is paid with its real hours.
AM3: Tags sit on people, rules on the cycle. Tick the tag a zone needs and the minimum per half, and the app enforces it everywhere: booking, claims, swaps, pre-fill, and your own cell editor, where you get a warning and Place anyway, logged. A half short of a tag turns red and says what it needs.
AM4: Any shift can carry its own start and finish. You set them from the roster cell for anyone; switch on Staff may set their own hours and your people set theirs when they book or afterwards, and you're told. Pay, the calendar, reminders and the board use the real hours; cover and shares still count the half.
AM5: Keep your year grid and import it before each cycle. Tick Treat any filled cell as unavailable first, it's never remembered, then choose the file. Read the confirm: the sheet it read and the number of blocks. Every mark becomes a whole day unavailable; a real leave code stays itself. Importing again never duplicates. Unavailable is not leave: no pay row, and a shift already placed that day stays until you change it.
D0: You won't run the roster. Here's what you'll see of it: the board, the fairness table, the whole hospital, and every change written down.
S2c: The text says the round is open. Open Book shifts and tap a day. At the top, AM or PM. Below it, one chip per zone: Open means it's yours to take, and a taken one shows who has it. Tap a zone, and it's booked, there and then. No basket, nothing to confirm. The receipt is the thing to look at: that's your share, booked. Add another day the same way. If a colleague tapped the same slot a moment before you, you're told at once, and you tap another. When the round closes, your admin publishes, and the whole roster lands on your phone.
A9: Some people work the same shifts every time. Open their card on Staff, then Pattern. A pattern can repeat every week, every fortnight, every four weeks, or by calendar month. Every four weeks gives you weeks A to D, and the heading says which cycle weeks each one covers. Calendar month is a list of rules: the first Wednesday, the last Saturday. The shift column is your own shift types, a full shift or an admin day included. Save it, then Commit to lock it, and the pattern places those shifts in every cycle. Now Roster, then Fixed cover. This is what the patterns alone would place, ghosted, with the cover row counted against your minimum. The weekday summary underneath is the recruiting brief: which days and halves the patterns cover to the minimum, and which never are. And the drift panel shows every fixed shift that now differs from its pattern: given away, swapped, on leave. The pattern is the promise; the roster is what happened.
AM6: Someone turns up to help who isn't on today's roster. With clocking on, a second switch on the Clock card lets them clock in anyway: Staff not rostered today may clock in. Their tap creates a casual shift for today in the zone they choose, and clocks them in. Nothing is paid on that tap alone. It lands under Hours to approve, flagged walk-in. Approve keeps the shift with the hours they clocked, for pay, the board and the calendar. Decline removes it, as if it never happened.
M5: If you are on a fixed pattern, your fixed shifts are already on the roster. Tap one on Book shifts and the day sheet says so. Can't make it? You have three ways. Offer it to the group: you stay on it until a colleague takes it, then you're off. Ask to come off, with a reason: your admin decides. Or Swap it with a colleague; your admin approves the swap. What you can't do is remove it outright. Your pattern itself stays as it was; to change it for good, change the pattern and send it for approval.
M6: Not rostered today, but you've come in to help? If your group allows it, My shifts shows Clock in, not rostered. Tap it, pick the half and the zone you're working, and Clock in. That makes a casual shift for today and clocks you in, by your phone's location or the poster. Clock out when you leave. Your admin approves the shift with the hours you clocked, and it reaches pay the same as any other.
